<!--
Every number in the text is computed inline from the small tables in
data/uncertainty_evidence/ (relative to this article). They are copies of the
tables that data-raw/uncertainty_evidence/90_article_tables.R writes from the
outputs of the other scripts in that directory, with evidence_numbers.parquet
pruned to the keys used here by
data-raw/uncertainty_evidence/91_bundle_article_data.R. Typed numbers are
definitions only (thresholds such as p < 0.01 or 0.95, design sizes such as
7 v 7). get_row() stops when a key is missing, so a renamed result cannot
silently drop a number from the text.
-->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
library(isoformic)
library(ggplot2)

data_dir <- "data/uncertainty_evidence"
ev <- read_parquet(file.path(data_dir, "evidence_numbers.parquet"))
flt1 <- read_parquet(file.path(data_dir, "flt1_isoforms.parquet"))
rep_flags <- read_parquet(file.path(data_dir, "replication_flags.parquet"))
story <- read_parquet(file.path(data_dir, "story_genes.parquet"))

get_row <- function(key) {
  r <- ev[ev$key == key, ]
  if (nrow(r) != 1L) {
    stop("evidence key not found or not unique: ", key, call. = FALSE)
  }
  r
}
val <- function(key) get_row(key)$estimate
num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f", big.mark = ",")
}
int <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
# fraction -> percent
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(num(100 * x, digits), "%")
# value already in percent
pc <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(num(x, digits), "%")
# the interval of a key, "lo to hi"
ci_range <- function(key, digits = 2, f = num) {
  r <- get_row(key)
  sprintf("%s to %s", f(r$ci_lo, digits), f(r$ci_hi, digits))
}
# estimate with its 95% CI
ci <- function(key, digits = 2, f = num) {
  sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s)", f(val(key), digits), ci_range(key, digits, f))
}
# adjusted rate ratio, top against bottom third of InfRV, pre-registered model
rr <- function(d, m) paste0("A.adj_rr.", d, ".", m, ".prereg.top")
rr_raw <- function(d, m) paste0("A.adj_rr_rawjk.", d, ".", m, ".prereg.top")
fl <- function(name) flt1[flt1$transcript_name == name, ]
cl <- function(k) paste0("B.cluster.cluster.", k)
pl <- function(flag) rep_flags[rep_flags$dataset == "placenta half-splits" & rep_flags$flag == flag, ]
```

Salmon and other quantifiers do not return one count per isoform.
They return a most likely count and a measure of how far that count could move,
here `r int(val("S0.n_draws"))` Gibbs draws per sample.
The [uncertainty article](isoformic-uncertainty.html) shows how `isoformic` turns the draws into
per-isoform summaries and a check of the direction of every call
(at the time of this evaluation it also gave every call a confidence class, since removed; see the end of [What we recommend](#what-we-recommend)).
That article works on a small panel of genes from two knockdown series in cell lines.
This one asks whether any of it changes the results of a genome-wide analysis of a real cohort.
The evaluation was planned in writing before any test was run,
and it reports what did not work as well as what did.
The plan fixed two decision rules, R-A and R-B (below); one failed and one passed only narrowly.
The result this article leads with, the sign agreement flag, was not one of them.
Only its threshold (0.95, the package default) was fixed in the plan;
the flag was one of several secondary flags that the analysis scripts defined before the replication was run,
and it was made the headline after the results were known.
The plan and its amendments are files in the package repository, not entries in an external registry,
and they were committed to it together with the results.
So the repository history does not show that the plan came first;
that rests on the time stamp written inside the plan, which also records the hash of the frozen package code it was run on.

**In short**

- **One check pays off: the sign of the fold-change across the draws.**
  In a real preeclampsia against control comparison, split in halves of the cohort
  (`r int(val("design.n_pe") / 2)` preeclampsia samples against 7 or 8 control units in each discovery half),
  `r pc(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.pct_flagged"))` of the transcript calls of the discovery halves (q < 0.10) have a fold-change
  whose sign changes in more than 5% of the draws (`sign_agreement` below 0.95);
  in the full cohort the share is `r pc(val("B.prevalence.F1.pct_sign_agree_lt_0.95"))`
  of the `r int(get_row("B.prevalence.F1.pct_sign_agree_lt_0.95")$n)` transcript calls at q < 0.05,
  since the halves, with fewer samples and a looser threshold, make more borderline calls.
  Those calls of the discovery halves replicate in the held-out half in
  `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_flagged"))` of cases, against
  `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_unflagged"))` for the other calls
  (adjusted odds ratio `r num(val(cl("gene.unstable_or")))`,
  95% CI `r ci_range(cl("gene.unstable_or"))` with genes resampled as clusters;
  the interval holds for this cohort and does not include the variation from the choice of samples).
  Setting them aside costs `r pc(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.replicated_calls_removed_pct"))`
  of the calls that do replicate.
  The check is narrow: it marks only `r pct(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.sensitivity_nonreplication"), 0)` of the calls that fail to replicate,
  and it is not a general screen for false positives. It sees only the uncertainty of the quantification,
  and in the null comparison below `r pct(val("A.m9class.7v7.share_calls_stable"), 0)` of the false calls
  had a fold-change whose sign was stable over the draws (7 v 7).
  This was a secondary analysis, not one of the plan's decision rules.
- **With few samples, uncertain isoforms collect more than their share of the nominal false positives.**
  With 3 or 5 samples per group, false calls at nominal p < 0.01 were
  `r num(val(rr("3v3", "M1")), 1)` and `r num(val(rr("5v5", "M1")), 1)` times as frequent
  in the most uncertain third of isoforms as in the best-determined third.
  At q < 0.05 false calls were rare
  (`r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.3v3.M1.own.all"))` per 3 v 3 split and `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.5v5.M1.own.all"))` per 5 v 5 split).
  With 7 per group no excess was detected (`r num(val(rr("7v7", "M1")))`; raw jackknife `r ci_range(rr_raw("7v7", "M1"))`, which still allows an excess of up to `r num(get_row(rr_raw("7v7", "M1"))$ci_hi)`, close to the `r num(val(rr("5v5", "M1")))` seen at 5 v 5, and overlaps the raw 5 v 5 interval, `r ci_range(rr_raw("5v5", "M1"))`),
  so the pre-registered rule R-A, judged at 7 per group, **failed**
  (the plan named no group size; the analysis used its largest design, as described below).
- **The former default confidence class is a weak filter, and the InfRV cut-off of 0.5 is too broad to be one.**
  The class (the package's default summary at the time) marks `r pc(val("B.flags.flag_primary.pct_flagged"), 0)` of the calls
  and separates replicating calls only modestly within cells of equal count and |z|
  (a gap of `r num(val("B.flags.flag_primary.matched_deficit"), 3)` in replication rate),
  so a filter on it would remove `r pc(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_primary.replicated_calls_removed_pct"), 0)` of the calls that replicate;
  the InfRV cut-off of 0.5 marks
  `r pct(val("S0.uncertain.TRUE") / val("S0.U.all"), 0)` of the expressed isoforms, so it was not tested as a flag in the placenta
  (in the read halves it marks about 90% of the calls, and several of its odds ratios are near separation).
- **Dividing the counts by the overdispersion is not free, and its effect on real data is unclear.**
  In the null with 3 or 5 samples per group it removes the concentration of nominal false calls in uncertain isoforms
  (there is none to remove with 7 per group), but not the false calls themselves, and with known changes added it finds fewer of those changes.
  In the real comparison it made more calls than point counts on the transcripts both tested
  (about as many when each applied its own expression filter);
  these data cannot say whether the extra calls are true.

## What the draws are, and what each flag means

A read that is compatible with several isoforms of a gene has to be shared out between them.
The quantifier finds the most likely split (the *point estimate*),
but other splits explain the reads almost as well.
Gibbs sampling draws plausible splits from that range:
each *draw* is a complete set of counts that the reads could have produced.
If an isoform has a similar count in every draw, the reads determine it;
if its count swings between draws, they do not.
The draws describe only this assignment uncertainty, not biological variability between samples.

The evaluation tests these summaries of the draws (all computed by `add_uncertainty()` and `de_confidence()`):

| Flag | What it says | Definition here |
|---|---|---|
| sign agreement below 0.95 | the direction of this call depends on how the reads are assigned | the fold-change of the contrast, repeated on each draw, has the sign of its median in fewer than 95% of the draws |
| top third of InfRV | the abundance of the isoform is poorly determined | inferential relative variance [@swish] in the highest third of the expressed isoforms |
| uncertain | the same, with a fixed cut-off | InfRV of at least 0.5 (the package default) |
| not identifiable | the reads cannot separate the isoform from another one, whatever the depth | its abundance is not fixed by the totals of the equivalence classes, in at least one sample |
| no unique reads | no read is compatible with this isoform alone | from the equivalence classes |
| ambiguous partner | another isoform of the gene takes reads from it | draws negatively correlated (at most -0.5) with a sibling |
| confidence class not `high` | the package's default summary at the time (since removed) | `high` needs sign agreement of at least 0.95, not uncertain, and no ambiguous partner |

*Divided counts* go one step further: the overdispersion that the read assignment adds to each
isoform is estimated from the draws, and the counts are divided by it before the test
[@baldoni2024], so that uncertain isoforms count for less.

## Data and design

**Placenta.** The main cohort is the placenta RNA-seq of @yang2020placenta
(GEO [GSE148241](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE148241),
BioProject [PRJNA622166](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA622166)):
`r int(val("design.n_pe"))` preeclampsia and `r int(val("design.n_control"))` control samples,
quantified with Salmon [@salmon] on GENCODE 50 [@gencode] with `r int(val("S0.n_draws"))` Gibbs draws per sample.
Two pairs of control samples are labelled as pairs (A and B) in GEO;
they are probably twin placentas and so not independent, and one member of each pair was kept,
leaving `r int(val("design.n_control_units"))` control units.
The analysis uses the `r int(val("S0.U.all"))` transcripts of `r int(val("S0.genes_U.all"))` genes
expressed in the preeclampsia samples.
The InfRV thirds (cut points `r num(val("S0.cut.infrv_tertile.low_mid"))` and
`r num(val("S0.cut.infrv_tertile.mid_high"))`) were also measured in the preeclampsia samples only,
so they do not depend on the control samples that the null splits use.

**Mouse.** The `r int(get_row("C.batch.batch1_short_fragments.frag_min")$n + get_row("C.batch.batch2.frag_min")$n)`
control males of a mouse brain study [@degroat2024]
(BioProject [PRJNA984605](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA984605)),
quantified on GENCODE vM39, give a second null in another species.

**Knockdown read halves.** The two knockdown series of the uncertainty article,
[GSE129540](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE129540) [@munkley2019] and
[GSE75489](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE75489) [@yang2016],
were split into random halves of the reads of each library and quantified again.
As a sensitivity check, GSE129540 was also analysed on the consecutive halves of the uncertainty article
(the first and second 6 million read pairs of each library; the rows "consecutive" in the table of the read halves below).
Here the calls of both kinds of halves are made at q < 0.10 in both directions (half A checked in half B, and B in A) and pooled,
so they number more than the 110 edgeR calls at FDR < 0.05 in half 1 reported in that article.

Two tests were written down before the results were known
(`data-raw/uncertainty_evidence/prereg.yaml` in the package repository);
a third, the mouse null, was added afterwards by analogy with the first (amendment A19):

1. **A null comparison.** Control placentas were split at random into two groups
   (3 v 3, 5 v 5 and 7 v 7, at least `r int(val("design.null_splits_per_size"))` splits per size).
   Nothing differs between the groups, so every call is false.
   Rule R-A asked that edgeR on the point counts make more false calls in the top third of InfRV
   than in the bottom third, that an uncertainty-aware method remove that excess,
   and that gene-level tests show no such excess.
   The plan named no group size for the rule.
   The analysis judged it at 7 v 7, the largest design and the one given the most splits
   (`r int(get_row(rr("7v7", "M1"))$n)`, each leaving out one control unit), set in an amendment made after a pilot.
   The pilot ran 3 null splits per size through every method to time them.
   It printed only timings and two validation checks (the swish control with 2 against 30 copies of the counts,
   and the confidence class of the scripts against the package), but it also wrote the null results of those 9 splits,
   which were kept as part of the full run; nothing records whether they were looked at before the amendment.
   That 7 v 7 decides the rule was written only in the analysis scripts and is recorded as a post hoc amendment.
2. **Held-out replication.** The real comparison was split into halves
   `r int(val("design.half_splits"))` times, each used in both directions
   (`r int(val("design.directed_pairs"))` directed pairs).
   A call made on one half (q < 0.10, a threshold set in the analysis scripts, not in the plan)
   *replicates* when the other half has the same sign at one-sided p < 0.05.
   Each flag is computed from the discovery half only,
   except "no unique reads", which uses all preeclampsia samples.
   Rule R-B asked that the default flag (class not `high`) predict non-replication,
   and do so better than a count-matched flag, which the plan described as having the same mean-count distribution.
   The analysis implemented that control as a flag of the same size made of the lowest-count calls of each pair,
   which is a different control; the departure was recorded only after the results.
   The plan listed two more controls, a placebo flag of the same size and a permutation baseline of the labels.
   The placebo was implemented as the default flag shuffled within cells of equal count and |z|,
   and the permutation baseline turned out not to be a null (both are reported below);
   neither change was recorded before the results.
   The plan registered only this one flag. Sign agreement, InfRV, identifiability, unique reads and
   ambiguous partners were secondary flags of the same analysis.
3. **The mouse null (not pre-registered)**, split 5 v 5 in all
   `r int(val("C.n_splits_batch_balanced") + val("C.n_splits_batch_aligned"))` possible ways.
   It applies the pre-registered R-A rule and model to a dataset that the plan does not name;
   its dataset, animals and split design were chosen without being registered,
   so it is an external check, not a pre-registered test.

The tests used edgeR quasi-likelihood [@edgerql] on point counts and on divided counts,
`swish` on the draws [@swish], and, for transcript usage, edgeR `diffSplice`, `satuRn` [@saturn] and `DEXSeq` [@dexseq].
The null also ran limma-voom on both kinds of counts (7 v 7 only), the DESeq2 Wald test on point counts
(`r int(get_row("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M5.own.all")$n)` splits at 7 v 7), a Wilcoxon test and gene-level edgeR;
the main text follows edgeR, and the [supplementary tables](#every-method-in-the-null) give every method.
Changes to the plan are recorded as amendments;
those made after the results were seen are marked as post hoc here and in
`data-raw/uncertainty_evidence/prereg_amendments.yaml`.

**Intervals.** All are 95% intervals, by part:
in the placenta null, a jackknife that leaves out one control unit
(with a Monte Carlo correction where it is valid; where the correction removes most of the variance, the uncorrected "raw" interval is given as well and is the conservative one);
in the mouse, the exact jackknife over all splits for each animal left out;
in the replication, the two-level bootstrap of the plan, called the *planned bootstrap* below:
half-splits, then the genes of each directed pair, with all the calls of a gene moving together
(the plan said transcripts within splits; resampling genes keeps the correlated calls of a gene together,
so its intervals should be no narrower than those of the plan, and the change is recorded as amendment A15).
The splits share samples, so intervals from a plain bootstrap over splits would be far too narrow.

## The result that holds: sign agreement predicts replication

```{r}
#| label: fig-replication
#| fig-cap: "Held-out replication of the transcript calls in the placenta half-splits, for the calls with and without each flag (pooled over the 60 directed pairs). The label gives the share of calls that the flag marks. A useful flag marks few calls whose replication is much lower. The two controls mark as many calls as the former default class: the lowest-count calls of each pair (the control R-B was judged on, as implemented), and the calls of lowest replication predicted from count and test statistic (post hoc)."
flag_label <- c(
  flag_unstable = "sign agreement < 0.95",
  flag_non_identifiable = "not identifiable",
  flag_infrv_top_tertile = "top third of InfRV",
  flag_zero_unique = "no unique reads",
  flag_ambiguous = "ambiguous partner",
  flag_primary = "class not high (former default)",
  flag_c4 = "control: lowest-count calls",
  flag_c4b = "control: count and |z| (post hoc)"
)
p <- rep_flags[rep_flags$dataset == "placenta half-splits" & rep_flags$flag %in% names(flag_label), ]
p <- p[match(names(flag_label), p$flag), ]
lab <- paste0(flag_label[p$flag], " (", num(p$pct_flagged, 1), "%)")
fig_rep <- rbind(
  data.frame(label = lab, group = "flagged", rate = p$rate_flagged),
  data.frame(label = lab, group = "not flagged", rate = p$rate_unflagged)
)
fig_rep$label <- factor(fig_rep$label, levels = rev(lab))
ggplot(fig_rep, aes(x = rate, y = label)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = label), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group), size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(flagged = "#C44E52", `not flagged` = "#4C72B0")) +
  labs(x = "Calls that replicate in the held-out half", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Over the `r int(val("design.directed_pairs"))` directed half-splits, edgeR on the discovery halves made
`r int(val("B.cluster.recur.calls"))` transcript calls, and
`r pct(val("B.2_secondary_outcomes.replication_rate"))` of them replicated.
The calls with sign agreement below 0.95:

| | |
|---|---|
| Share of calls flagged | `r pc(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.pct_flagged"))` |
| Replicate, flagged against not flagged | `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_flagged"))` against `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_unflagged"))` |
| Difference within cells of equal count and test statistic (post hoc) | `r num(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.matched_deficit"), 3)`; 95% CI `r ci_range("B.flags.flag_unstable.matched_deficit", 3)` (planned bootstrap, too narrow; see below) |
| Adjusted odds ratio of replication | `r num(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.adjusted_or"))`; 95% CI `r ci_range(cl("gene.unstable_or"))` (genes as clusters), `r ci_range("B.flags.flag_unstable.adjusted_or")` (planned bootstrap) |
| Flagged calls that fail to replicate | `r pct(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.PPV_nonreplication"), 0)` (all calls: `r pct(1 - val("B.2_secondary_outcomes.replication_rate"), 0)`) |
| Share of all failures it catches | `r pct(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.sensitivity_nonreplication"), 0)` |
| Replicating calls it would remove | `r pc(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.replicated_calls_removed_pct"))` |

The odds ratio is adjusted for the count, the test statistic (|z|), the number of isoforms of the gene and the transcript type.
The flag is narrow, so it catches few of the calls that fail; what it marks, though, mostly fails, at a small cost.

**How robust is it?**

- **It is not just low power.** Flagged calls have fewer reads (median about
  `r int(2^val("B.posthoc.power.median_log2_count.flag_unstable") - 0.5)` against
  `r int(2^val("B.posthoc.power.median_log2_count.not_flag_unstable") - 0.5)` mean reads), and replication depends on power.
  But the difference survives matching on count and |z| (table above),
  flexible splines on both (odds ratio `r num(val("B.posthoc.power.flag_unstable.replicated.or_splines"))`, post hoc),
  and fixed effects for each directed pair (`r num(val("B.cluster.pair_fe.flag_unstable.replicated.adjusted_or"))`, post hoc).
  At the same size, it also beats flags made of the lowest-count calls, the lowest-|z| calls
  and the calls with the lowest replication predicted from count and |z| (post hoc):
  a replication gap of `r num(val("B.posthoc.same_size.flag_unstable.deficit"), 3)` against
  `r num(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_count.deficit"), 3)`, `r num(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_absz.deficit"), 3)`
  and `r num(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_predicted_count_absz.deficit"), 3)`,
  `r pct(val("B.posthoc.same_size.flag_unstable.sensitivity_nonreplication"))` of the failures caught against
  `r pct(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_count.sensitivity_nonreplication"))`, `r pct(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_absz.sensitivity_nonreplication"))`
  and `r pct(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_predicted_count_absz.sensitivity_nonreplication"))`,
  and a larger gap in `r int(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_count.pairs_unstable_larger_deficit"))`,
  `r int(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_absz.pairs_unstable_larger_deficit"))`
  and `r int(val("B.posthoc.same_size.lowest_predicted_count_absz.pairs_unstable_larger_deficit"))`
  of the `r int(val("B.cluster.pairs.n"))` directed pairs.
- **It holds in every directed pair (raw rates).** Flagged calls replicate less in
  `r int(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.n_flagged_lower"))` of the `r int(val("B.cluster.pairs.n"))` directed pairs
  (flagged `r pct(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.rate_flagged_min"))` to `r pct(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.rate_flagged_max"))`,
  not flagged `r pct(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.rate_unflagged_min"))` to `r pct(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.rate_unflagged_max"))`).
- **The rates are specific to this design.** The `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_flagged"))` and
  `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_unflagged"))` above are pooled over the pairs.
  The pairs differ a lot: a discovery half made `r int(val("B.cluster.pairs.calls_min"))` to
  `r int(val("B.cluster.pairs.calls_max"))` calls, and the more calls a half made, the fewer replicated
  (correlation `r num(val("B.cluster.pairs.cor_calls_rate"))` over pairs).
  Pooling weights the large, low-replication pairs most; with every pair weighted equally the rates are
  `r pct(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.rate_flagged_mean"))` against `r pct(val("B.cluster.pairs.unstable.rate_unflagged_mean"))`.
  Read them as rates of this half-split design, not as probabilities that a call is true.
- **The same transcripts recur.** The `r int(val("B.cluster.recur.unstable.calls"))` flagged calls come from
  `r int(val("B.cluster.recur.unstable.transcripts"))` transcripts in `r int(val("B.cluster.recur.unstable.genes"))` genes,
  because all half-splits draw on the same `r int(val("design.n_pe") + val("design.n_control_units"))` samples.
  The planned bootstrap resampled genes separately in each pair and so gives intervals that are too narrow
  (`r ci_range("B.flags.flag_unstable.adjusted_or")`);
  resampling each gene once over all pairs gives `r ci_range(cl("gene.unstable_or"))`,
  and crossing that with the half-splits `r ci_range(cl("split_x_gene.unstable_or"))` (post hoc).
  Either way the odds ratio stays far below 1.
  Neither scheme resamples the samples themselves, so both intervals hold for this cohort of
  `r int(val("design.n_pe") + val("design.n_control_units"))` samples;
  the rates of single pairs (above) show how much one split of it can differ from another.
- **The direction itself replicates less.** With "same sign in the held-out half" as the outcome (post hoc),
  which needs less power than p < 0.05, the odds ratio is
  `r num(val("B.signconc.flag_unstable.adjusted_or"))` (95% CI `r ci_range(cl("gene.unstable_or_signconc"))`, genes as clusters):
  `r pct(val("B.signconc.flag_unstable.sign_concordance_flagged"))` of flagged calls keep their sign, against
  `r pct(val("B.signconc.flag_unstable.sign_concordance_unflagged"))`.
  This outcome is not free of power either: among unflagged calls it rises from
  `r num(val("B.posthoc.power.unflagged.sign_concordant.by_d_absz_decile.1"), 3)` to
  `r num(val("B.posthoc.power.unflagged.sign_concordant.by_d_absz_decile.10"), 3)` from the lowest to the highest decile of |z|.
- **Technical read halves agree.** In the two knockdown series, calls made on one random half of the reads
  were checked in the other half. The odds ratio of the same flag is
  `r ci("R.random.GSE129540.M1.flag_unstable.adjusted_or", 3)` for GSE129540 and
  `r ci("R.random.GSE75489.M1.flag_unstable.adjusted_or", 3)` for GSE75489.
  This is a favourable consistency check, not an independent replication:
  the two halves share the libraries and all their biology and differ only by the sampling and assignment noise
  that the draws model. The calls are few (`r int(val("R.random.GSE129540.M1.flag_unstable.n_calls"))` and
  `r int(val("R.random.GSE75489.M1.flag_unstable.n_calls"))`), the flag marks far more of them than in the placenta
  (`r pc(val("R.random.GSE129540.M1.flag_unstable.pct_flagged"), 0)` and `r pc(val("R.random.GSE75489.M1.flag_unstable.pct_flagged"), 0)`),
  and in GSE75489 only `r int(val("B.cluster.rhalf.random_GSE75489_M1_AB.n_calls_q10"))` and
  `r int(val("B.cluster.rhalf.random_GSE75489_M1_BA.n_calls_q10"))` transcripts passed q < 0.10,
  so the test fell back on the 500 lowest p-values in each direction, most of them not significant
  (a fallback written into the analysis scripts, like the q < 0.10 threshold; the read halves are not in the plan).
  Sign agreement is not special there: with the same adjustment as in the placenta,
  every flag of the read halves has an odds ratio well below 1, several of them lower than sign agreement (table below).
  The read halves therefore support the general point that the draws carry information about which calls repeat,
  not sign agreement in particular.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rhalf-flags
rh_label <- c(
  flag_unstable = "sign agreement < 0.95",
  flag_infrv_tertile = "top third of InfRV",
  flag_uncertain = "uncertain (InfRV >= 0.5)",
  flag_ambiguous = "ambiguous partner"
)
rh <- rep_flags[startsWith(rep_flags$dataset, "read halves") & rep_flags$flag %in% names(rh_label), ]
rh <- rh[order(rh$dataset, match(rh$flag, names(rh_label))), ]
# odds ratios that are near separation are printed as an upper bound
or_fmt <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0.001, "< 0.001", num(x, 3))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Series = sub("read halves ", "", rh$dataset, fixed = TRUE),
    Flag = rh_label[rh$flag],
    Calls = int(rh$n_calls),
    `Share flagged` = paste0(num(rh$pct_flagged, 0), "%"),
    `Replicate, flagged against not flagged` = paste(pct(rh$rate_flagged, 0), "against", pct(rh$rate_unflagged, 0)),
    `Adjusted odds ratio (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", or_fmt(rh$adjusted_or), or_fmt(rh$or_lo), or_fmt(rh$or_hi)),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: rhalf-numbers
rh_cell <- function(d, f) rh[rh$dataset == paste("read halves", d) & rh$flag == f, ]
```

The InfRV and "uncertain" flags mark most of the calls in the read halves, so several of their odds ratios are near separation and unstable.
The ambiguous partner marks few calls, and its raw replication rates hardly differ from those of the other calls,
but once count and |z| are accounted for its odds ratio is `r num(rh_cell("GSE75489 random", "flag_ambiguous")$adjusted_or)` in GSE75489
and `r num(rh_cell("GSE129540 random", "flag_ambiguous")$adjusted_or)` in GSE129540 (random halves),
against `r num(pl("flag_ambiguous")$adjusted_or)` in the placenta.
Which flag predicts best depends on the data; only the placenta half-splits, a biological comparison, put sign agreement first, by odds ratio and by replication gap.

```{r}
#| label: non-identifiable-numbers
# Share of the failures and of the replicating calls that the flag marks,
# from its share of calls and its replication rates
ni_p <- val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.pct_flagged") / 100
ni_f <- val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.rate_flagged")
ni_u <- val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.rate_unflagged")
```

In the placenta, other flags carry less.
Non-identifiable calls (`r pc(val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.pct_flagged"))` of the calls) replicate in
`r pct(val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.rate_flagged"))` against `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.rate_unflagged"))`
(odds ratio `r num(val("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.adjusted_or"))`, 95% CI `r ci_range("B.flags.flag_non_identifiable.adjusted_or")` from the planned bootstrap).
It is a broader but weaker descriptor than sign agreement:
it covers `r pct(ni_p * (1 - ni_f) / (ni_p * (1 - ni_f) + (1 - ni_p) * (1 - ni_u)), 0)` of the calls that fail to replicate
(against `r pct(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.sensitivity_nonreplication"), 0)` for an unstable direction),
but also `r pct(ni_p * ni_f / (ni_p * ni_f + (1 - ni_p) * ni_u), 0)` of those that replicate,
so it can be reported next to `sign_agreement` as a description, not used as a filter.
The top third of InfRV and the absence of unique reads have odds ratios of
`r num(val("B.flags.flag_infrv_top_tertile.adjusted_or"))` and `r num(val("B.flags.flag_zero_unique.adjusted_or"))`,
and an ambiguous partner predicts little (`r num(val("B.flags.flag_ambiguous.adjusted_or"))`).

## What did not work

### The pre-registered null rule fails at 7 v 7

```{r}
#| label: fig-null-rr
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Rate of false calls (p < 0.01) in the top third of InfRV against the bottom third, adjusted for expression decile and number of isoforms in the gene (the pre-registered model). Above 1, uncertain isoforms collect more false calls. Placenta: control placentas only, by group size; mouse: control males, 5 v 5, all splits and the splits balanced for a library batch. Bars: 95% jackknife intervals; for the placenta the uncorrected (raw) jackknife, the conservative one."
methods <- c(M1 = "edgeR, point counts", M2 = "edgeR, divided counts", M6 = "swish, draws")
rows <- list()
for (d in c("3v3", "5v5", "7v7")) {
  for (m in names(methods)) {
    # swish (M6) was not run at 3 v 3
    if (!any(ev$key == rr_raw(d, m))) {
      next
    }
    r <- get_row(rr_raw(d, m))
    rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
      dataset = "placenta", design = d, method = methods[[m]],
      estimate = r$estimate, lo = r$ci_lo, hi = r$ci_hi
    )
  }
}
for (s in c("", "_batch_balanced")) {
  for (m in names(methods)) {
    r <- get_row(paste0("C.", m, ".adjusted_rate_ratio_high_low", s))
    rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
      dataset = "mouse", design = if (nzchar(s)) "5v5, balanced" else "5v5, all",
      method = methods[[m]], estimate = r$estimate, lo = r$ci_lo, hi = r$ci_hi
    )
  }
}
fig_rr <- do.call(rbind, rows)
fig_rr$design <- factor(fig_rr$design, levels = rev(c("3v3", "5v5", "7v7", "5v5, all", "5v5, balanced")))
fig_rr$method <- factor(fig_rr$method, levels = methods)
ggplot(fig_rr, aes(x = estimate, y = design, colour = method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4C72B0", "#DD8452", "#55A868")) +
  facet_grid(dataset ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Rate ratio, top against bottom third of InfRV (log scale)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

At 7 v 7, the size at which the analysis judged the rule, false calls of edgeR on point counts were **not detectably**
more frequent in uncertain isoforms: the adjusted rate ratio is `r num(val(rr("7v7", "M1")))`
(95% CI with the raw jackknife `r ci_range(rr_raw("7v7", "M1"))`; the Monte Carlo corrected `r ci_range(rr("7v7", "M1"))` keeps only about `r pct((log(get_row(rr("7v7", "M1"))$ci_hi / get_row(rr("7v7", "M1"))$ci_lo) / log(get_row(rr_raw("7v7", "M1"))$ci_hi / get_row(rr_raw("7v7", "M1"))$ci_lo))^2, 0)` of the jackknife variance, a remainder within the noise of the Monte Carlo estimate, so it is not reliable), so R-A fails.
Its other criteria cannot rescue it: there is no excess to remove
(the ratio of divided to point counts is `r num(val("A.rr_ratio.7v7.prereg.M2_vs_M1"))`, 95% CI `r ci_range("A.rr_ratio.7v7.prereg.M2_vs_M1")`).
Point counts were calibrated at this size:
`r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M1.own.all"), 3)` false calls per split at q < 0.05,
and an observed share at p < 0.01 of `r num(val("A.inflation_p01.7v7.M1.own.all"))` times the expected one
(95% CI `r ci_range("A.inflation_p01.7v7.M1.own.all")`).
That holds for edgeR's quasi-likelihood test, not for every test of the same counts:
the DESeq2 Wald test made `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M5.own.all"), 1)` false calls per split at q < 0.05
on `r int(get_row("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M5.own.all")$n)` of the 7 v 7 splits
(raw jackknife interval `r ci_range("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M5.own.all", 1)`;
observed over expected share at p < 0.01 `r num(val("A.inflation_p01.7v7.M5.own.all"))`,
95% CI `r ci_range("A.inflation_p01.7v7.M5.own.all")`),
while limma-voom made `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M3.own.all"), 3)`
([supplementary tables](#every-method-in-the-null)).
A sensitivity model that also adjusts for identifiability (not pre-registered) gives
`r num(val("A.adj_rr.7v7.M1.ident.top"))`, the same conclusion.

**With fewer samples per group the excess appears** (secondary results: the plan listed these sizes, but the analysis did not judge R-A on them).
The adjusted rate ratio is `r num(val(rr("5v5", "M1")))` at 5 v 5
(raw jackknife `r ci_range(rr_raw("5v5", "M1"))`) and `r ci(rr("3v3", "M1"))` at 3 v 3.
The false calls are not more numerous overall
(at 3 v 3 the observed share at p < 0.01 is `r num(val("A.inflation_p01.3v3.M1.own.all"))` times the expected one,
95% CI `r ci_range("A.inflation_p01.3v3.M1.own.all")`);
they fall more often on uncertain isoforms
(`r num(val("A.inflation_p01.3v3.M1.own.tertile_high"))` in the top third against
`r num(val("A.inflation_p01.3v3.M1.own.tertile_low"))` in the bottom third).
It is not explained by differences in mapping rate between the groups
(at 3 v 3 the ratio is `r num(val("A.tertile_rr_by_mapping.3v3.M1.low"))` in splits with a small difference in mapping rate and
`r num(val("A.tertile_rr_by_mapping.3v3.M1.high"))` with a large one).

**The mouse null agrees with the small-sample placenta result, with caveats.**
Mouse controls at 5 v 5 give `r ci("C.RA.all.m1_adj_rr")`, in the same direction as the placenta at the same size
(`r num(val(rr("5v5", "M1")))`);
divided counts and `swish` reduce it, and gene-level tests show no excess
(`r num(val("C.RA.all.m11_adj_rr"))`, 95% CI `r ci_range("C.RA.all.m11_adj_rr")`).
Read with the pre-registered R-A rule, it passes only with an exact jackknife over all splits per animal and a reading of the gene-level criterion that the plan did not spell out (amendment A8).
The mouse design itself was not pre-registered (amendment A19), so this is supporting evidence, not a confirmatory test.
The mouse controls also turned out to hold two library batches
(mean fragment lengths `r num(val("C.batch.batch1_short_fragments.frag_min"), 0)` to
`r num(val("C.batch.batch1_short_fragments.frag_max"), 0)` bp against
`r num(val("C.batch.batch2.frag_min"), 0)` to `r num(val("C.batch.batch2.frag_max"), 0)` bp):
of the `r int(val("C.n_splits_batch_aligned"))` splits that line up with the batch,
`r n_al <- round(val("C.n_splits_batch_aligned") * val("C.M1.splits_with_any_call_q05_U_batch_aligned")); if (n_al == 1) "only one" else int(n_al)` made false calls on point counts at q < 0.05:
the split that puts the `r int(get_row("C.batch.batch1_short_fragments.frag_min")$n)` animals of the short-fragment batch in one group,
with `r int(val("C.M1.false_calls_q05_U_per_split_batch_aligned") * val("C.n_splits_batch_aligned"))` calls.
The other `r int(val("C.n_splits_batch_aligned") * (1 - val("C.M1.splits_with_any_call_q05_U_batch_aligned")))` made none,
and the `r int(val("C.n_splits_batch_balanced"))` balanced splits made `r num(val("C.M1.false_calls_q05_U_per_split_batch_balanced"))` per split.
On the balanced splits alone the ratio is `r ci("C.RA.batch_balanced.m1_adj_rr")`.

### The former default confidence class is a weak filter

The pre-registered flag, class other than `high`, marks `r pc(val("B.flags.flag_primary.pct_flagged"))` of the calls.
They replicate somewhat less (`r pct(val("B.flags.flag_primary.rate_flagged"))` against
`r pct(val("B.flags.flag_primary.rate_unflagged"))`; odds ratio `r num(val("B.flags.flag_primary.adjusted_or"))`,
95% CI `r ci_range("B.flags.flag_primary.adjusted_or")`, or `r ci_range(cl("gene.primary_or"))` with genes as clusters).
Rule R-B also asked it to beat a count-matched flag.
As implemented, that control is a flag of the same size made of the lowest-count calls of each pair,
not the flag with the same count distribution that the plan described (a post hoc amendment records the difference).
The class beat it by `r num(val("B.3_C4_count_matched.deficit_primary_minus_deficit_C4"), 3)` in replication rate,
95% CI `r ci_range("B.3_C4_count_matched.deficit_primary_minus_deficit_C4", 3)` under the planned bootstrap,
so **R-B passes formally, but the pass is fragile**:
with genes resampled as clusters across the half-splits (post hoc) the interval is
`r ci_range(cl("gene.primary_minus_c4"), 3)`, and it includes 0.
A same-size flag built from count and |z| alone (post hoc) separates much better than the class:
its gap in replication is `r num(val("B.flags.flag_c4b.deficit"), 3)` against
`r num(val("B.flags.flag_primary.deficit"), 3)`.
Closer to the control the plan described, the class keeps a gap within cells of equal count and |z|
(gap `r num(val("B.flags.flag_primary.matched_deficit"), 3)`, 95% CI `r ci_range("B.flags.flag_primary.matched_deficit", 3)`, planned bootstrap; the matched gap itself is post hoc),
while the class shuffled within those cells, which has nearly the same count distribution by construction, has a gap of
`r num(val("B.2_placebo_flag.deficit_placebo_mean"), 3)` (`r ci_range("B.2_placebo_flag.deficit_placebo_mean", 3)` over the shuffles).
That shuffle is how the analysis implemented the plan's placebo flag, which the plan described only as a random flag of the same size in each split.
The plan's last control, a permutation baseline of the labels, turned out not to be a null.
It relabelled the samples of the discovery half 100 times, but a discovery half holds only
`r int(val("design.n_pe") / 2)` preeclampsia samples, so every permutation kept part of the real contrast or reversed it.
Under the permuted labels the calls replicated in `r pct(val("B.2_C1_permutation.replication_rate_label_permuted"))` of cases
(against `r pct(val("B.2_C1_permutation.replication_rate_observed"))` with the true labels),
and the class separated them by `r num(val("B.2_C1_permutation.deficit_primary_label_permuted"), 3)`,
no less than with the true labels (`r num(val("B.flags.flag_primary.deficit"), 3)`;
difference `r num(val("B.2_C1_permutation.excess_deficit_over_C1"), 3)`, 95% CI `r ci_range("B.2_C1_permutation.excess_deficit_over_C1", 3)` under the planned bootstrap).
That gap shrank as more samples were relabelled, from `r num(val("B.2_C1_by_n_relabelled.deficit_n_relabelled_2"), 3)` with 2
to `r num(val("B.2_C1_by_n_relabelled.deficit_n_relabelled_8"), 3)` with 8, so it follows the real contrast left in the permutations.
Read literally, this control would say that the class separates calls no better under the true labels than under permuted ones;
because the permutations are not nulls, it cannot be used either for or against the class, and the analysis did not use it.
These comparisons were not the rule as run, and they do not change the verdict on R-B.
Used as a filter, the class would remove `r pc(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_primary.replicated_calls_removed_pct"), 0)`
of the calls that replicate.

In the null the class did not help to pick out the false calls.
The `high` class holds `r pct(val("A.m9class.7v7.share_tested_high"))` of the tested transcripts but
`r pct(val("A.m9class.7v7.share_calls_high"))` of the false calls at p < 0.01 (7 v 7; enrichment `r num(val("A.m9class.7v7.enrichment_calls_in_high"))`,
95% CI `r ci_range("A.m9class.7v7.enrichment_calls_in_high")`).
This excess is not an inversion of the class: it is what any summary of the direction over the draws shows once calls are selected by their p-value.
A call at p < 0.01 has a large fold-change, so its sign is stable over the draws whether the call is true or false,
while most tested transcripts have a fold-change near 0 and an unstable sign.
A stable direction alone holds `r pct(val("A.m9class.7v7.share_tested_stable"), 0)` of the tested transcripts
and `r pct(val("A.m9class.7v7.share_calls_stable"), 0)` of the null calls
(enrichment `r num(val("A.m9class.7v7.enrichment_calls_in_stable"))`, 95% CI `r ci_range("A.m9class.7v7.enrichment_calls_in_stable")`):
the draws describe the quantification, and a false call driven by biological noise is stable over them.
The test that bears on the class as a filter is the removal at equal cost.
Keeping only class `high` removes `r pct(val("A.m9class.7v7.share_tested_removed_by_M9a"))` of the tested transcripts,
and at equal removal it is no better than dropping the least expressed ones
(difference in the share of false calls removed `r num(val("A.m9_vs_m10.7v7.common.a.removed_M9_minus_M10"))`,
95% CI `r ci_range("A.m9_vs_m10.7v7.common.a.removed_M9_minus_M10")`).

### The InfRV cut-off of 0.5 marks almost everything

Of the expressed placenta transcripts, `r pct(val("S0.uncertain.TRUE") / val("S0.U.all"))` have InfRV of at least 0.5,
`r pct(val("S0.non_identifiable.TRUE") / val("S0.U.all"))` are not identifiable in at least one sample,
and `r pct(val("S0.zero_unique.TRUE") / val("S0.U.all"))` have no read of their own;
`r pct(val("S0.isoform_bin.10+") / val("S0.U.all"))` are in genes with 10 or more annotated isoforms.
The bottom third of InfRV ends at `r num(val("S0.cut.infrv_tertile.low_mid"))`,
`r num(val("S0.cut.infrv_tertile.low_mid") / 0.5, 1)` times the cut-off,
so on a genome-wide human annotation the cut-off separates almost nothing.
The thirds themselves are stable: computed from 15 draws instead of 30,
`r pct(val("S0.tertile_agreement_15_vs_30"))` of the transcripts stay in the same third.

### Dividing the counts costs power and does not remove false discoveries

Dividing the counts by the overdispersion removes the small-sample concentration of nominal false calls in uncertain isoforms:
the ratio of the rate ratios (divided over point counts) is
`r ci("A.rr_ratio.5v5.prereg.M2_vs_M1")` at 5 v 5 and `r ci("A.rr_ratio.3v3.prereg.M2_vs_M1")` at 3 v 3
(`r ci("A.rr_ratio.7v7.prereg.M2_vs_M1")` at 7 v 7, where there was no excess to remove).
It does not lower the number of false discoveries.
At q < 0.05, point counts made `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.3v3.M1.own.all"))` false calls per 3 v 3 split
and divided counts `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.3v3.M2.own.all"))`
(`r num(val("A.tail.3v3.M2.own.mean_q05_without_max_split"))` without their worst split);
at 7 v 7, `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M1.own.all"), 3)` against `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M2.own.all"))`,
`r pct(val("A.tail.7v7.M2.own.share_from_max_split"), 0)` of them from a single split.
Divided counts also test fewer transcripts
(`r int(val("A.tail.7v7.M2.own.mean_tested"))` per 7 v 7 split against `r int(val("A.tail.7v7.M1.own.mean_tested"))`).

To measure power, known changes were added to
`r int(get_row("A.thin.7v7_louo.M1.all.q_0.05.fdr_pooled")$n)` of the 7 v 7 null splits
(and as many 5 v 5 splits, in the supplementary tables):
5% of the genes with several isoforms (sampled within each third of InfRV) and as many single-isoform genes
were thinned, each gene in one of the two groups (chosen at random) and by its own factor of 1.5 to 4
(log2 fold-change drawn between 0.58 and 2), the same factor for every isoform of the gene.
This keeps the isoform ratios, so it measures power and the false discovery rate between genes,
not misattribution between isoforms. At q < 0.05:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-thinning
thin_method <- c(
  M1 = "edgeR, point counts",
  M2 = "edgeR, divided counts",
  M6 = "swish, draws",
  M9a = "edgeR, then keep class high only"
)
thin_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(thin_method), function(m) {
  base <- paste0("A.thin.7v7_louo.", m, ".all.q_0.05.")
  top <- paste0("A.thin.7v7_louo.", m, ".top_tertile.q_0.05.")
  data.frame(
    Method = thin_method[[m]],
    `Empirical FDR` = ci(paste0(base, "fdr_pooled"), 3),
    `True calls` = int(val(paste0(base, "total_calls")) - val(paste0(base, "total_false"))),
    `True calls, top third of InfRV` = int(val(paste0(top, "total_calls")) - val(paste0(top, "total_false"))),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(thin_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: thin-fdr-range
thin_fdr <- sapply(names(thin_method), function(m) val(paste0("A.thin.7v7_louo.", m, ".all.q_0.05.fdr_pooled")))
thin_fdr_hi <- sapply(c("M2", "M6"), function(m) get_row(paste0("A.thin.7v7_louo.", m, ".all.q_0.05.fdr_pooled"))$ci_hi)
```

For the four methods in the table, the empirical false discovery rate at q < 0.05 lies between `r pct(min(thin_fdr), 0)` and `r pct(max(thin_fdr), 0)`:
below 5% for point counts and for keeping class `high` only, above it for divided counts and `swish`,
whose intervals are wide (upper ends `r pct(thin_fdr_hi[["M2"]], 0)` and `r pct(thin_fdr_hi[["M6"]], 0)`).
At an equal number of calls, the number divided counts make in each split, point counts had the lower false discovery rate
(`r num(val("A.thin.7v7_louo.M1.all.top_k_M2.fdr_pooled"), 3)` against `r num(val("A.thin.7v7_louo.M2.all.top_k_M2.fdr_pooled"), 3)`).
Point counts find the most true changes, and the gap is largest in the top third of InfRV,
where divided counts and `swish` lose most of their power and keeping class `high` removes nearly every call.
`swish` also behaves differently in the null: it makes fewer false calls in uncertain isoforms than in certain ones
(placenta 7 v 7 `r ci(rr("7v7", "M6"))`; mouse `r ci("C.M6.adjusted_rate_ratio_high_low")`),
which is the method working as designed but is the same loss of power seen from the other side,
and it was the only expression test with frequent false calls on the batch-balanced mouse splits
(at least one call at q < 0.05 in `r pct(val("C.M6.splits_with_any_call_q05_U_batch_balanced"), 0)` of them).
It made more false calls than point counts in the placenta too:
`r ci("A.mean_calls_q05.5v5.M6.own.all")` per 5 v 5 split at q < 0.05 against
`r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.5v5.M1.own.all"))` for edgeR on point counts,
and `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M6.own.all"))` against `r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M1.own.all"), 3)` at 7 v 7.

```{r}
#| label: od-numbers
d_raw <- function(set, stat) {
  val(paste0(
    "D.impact.placenta_8_PE_vs_15_control_units_DTE_edgeR_QL.raw_counts_-_divided_counts_genome-wide_prior.",
    set, ".", stat
  ))
}
d_kd <- function(series, stat) {
  val(paste0(
    "D.impact.", series, "_DTE_edgeR_QL_divided_counts.panel_prior_-_genome_prior_swapped.common.", stat
  ))
}
d_pl <- function(stat) {
  val(paste0(
    "D.impact.placenta_8_PE_vs_15_control_units_DTE_edgeR_QL_divided_counts.genome_prior_-_panel_median.common.", stat
  ))
}
kd_changed <- d_kd("GSE129540", "n_lost") + d_kd("GSE129540", "n_gained") +
  d_kd("GSE75489", "n_lost") + d_kd("GSE75489", "n_gained")
```

**In the real comparison divided counts made about as many calls or more.**
The overdispersion part of the evaluation also ran edgeR on the whole placenta comparison
(`r int(val("design.n_pe"))` preeclampsia samples against `r int(val("design.n_control_units"))` control units).
Each with its own expression filter, point counts made `r int(d_raw("separate", "n_calls_reference"))` calls at q < 0.05
and divided counts `r int(d_raw("separate", "n_calls_alternative"))`.
Refitted together on the `r int(d_raw("common", "n_tested_both"))` transcripts that both filters kept,
point counts made `r int(d_raw("common", "n_calls_reference"))` calls and divided counts `r int(d_raw("common", "n_calls_alternative"))`
(`r int(d_raw("common", "n_lost"))` lost, `r int(d_raw("common", "n_gained"))` gained);
point counts make up the difference by testing transcripts that division pushes below the filter.
A real comparison has no known truth, so these data cannot say whether the extra calls of divided counts are true changes;
the power arm above measured changes of whole genes in 7 v 7 null splits, a different setting, and does not settle it.
This check read the Salmon counts directly, without folding the copies of transcripts on alternate haplotypes,
so its numbers of calls differ from those of the main analysis.
The prior of the overdispersion mattered little.
The draws bundled for the knockdown panels give a prior `r num(val("D.3_HEADLINE_GSE129540_ratio_panel_prior_genome-wide_prior"), 1)` and
`r num(val("D.3_HEADLINE_GSE75489_ratio_panel_prior_genome-wide_prior"), 1)` times the genome-wide one,
yet using the genome-wide prior changed `r if (kd_changed == 0) "no" else int(kd_changed)` knockdown call on the transcripts both runs tested;
in the placenta, replacing the genome-wide prior with that of a median random panel of 39 genes moved the calls
from `r int(d_pl("n_calls_reference"))` to `r int(d_pl("n_calls_alternative"))`.

### Transcript usage

For `diffSplice`, divided counts help at 5 v 5
(`r num(val("A.dtu.diffsplice.5v5.raw.mean_n_genes_q05"))` false genes per split on point counts against
`r num(val("A.dtu.diffsplice.5v5.scaled.mean_n_genes_q05"))`), while at 7 v 7 both are low
(`r num(val("A.dtu.diffsplice.7v7_louo.raw.mean_n_genes_q05"))` and `r num(val("A.dtu.diffsplice.7v7_louo.scaled.mean_n_genes_q05"))`).
For `satuRn` the observed over expected share at p < 0.01 rose from
`r ci("A.dtu.satuRn.7v7_louo.raw.gene_inflation_p01")` on point counts to
`r ci("A.dtu.satuRn.7v7_louo.scaled.gene_inflation_p01")` on divided counts
(`r int(get_row("A.dtu.satuRn.7v7_louo.raw.gene_inflation_p01")$n)` splits);
the intervals overlap almost entirely, so these splits cannot tell the two apart,
and `DEXSeq` made many false calls either way
(`r num(val("A.dtu.DEXSeq.7v7_louo.raw.mean_n_genes_q05"), 1)` and `r num(val("A.dtu.DEXSeq.7v7_louo.scaled.mean_n_genes_q05"), 1)`
genes per split, `r int(get_row("A.dtu.DEXSeq.7v7_louo.raw.mean_n_genes_q05")$n)` splits only).
Tests of the productive fraction made almost no false calls either way
(`r num(val("A.nmd.raw.mean_n_padj05"), 3)` and `r num(val("A.nmd.divided.mean_n_padj05"), 3)` genes per 7 v 7 split).

## The genes named in the plan

The plan named FLT1 as its isoform-level example, ENG and LEP as its gene-level examples,
and two rules to pick one fragile and one robust gene from the results. All of them are reported here.
The classes `high`, `moderate` and `low` in this section are the confidence classes of the evaluated snapshot of the package,
which the current version no longer computes.

### FLT1

FLT1, whose soluble form is raised in preeclampsia, was the plan's isoform-level example.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flt1
f <- flt1[flt1$tested_edgeR %in% TRUE, ]
f <- f[order(-f$mean_count), ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Isoform = f$transcript_name,
    `Mean count` = int(f$mean_count),
    InfRV = num(f$mean_inf_rv, 1),
    `log2FC, point counts` = num(f$naive_log2FC),
    `log2FC, refit on each draw (2.5% to 97.5%)` = paste(num(f$draw_refit_lo), "to", num(f$draw_refit_hi)),
    `Class (snapshot)` = f$confidence,
    `Replicated when called` = paste0(pct(f$replicated_when_called, 0), " of ", f$n_called_discovery),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: flt1-numbers
mod <- f[f$confidence == "moderate", ]
# point estimate outside the 2.5-97.5% range of the per-draw refits, and
# further from zero than the whole range
outside_range <- function(x) x$naive_log2FC < x$draw_refit_lo | x$naive_log2FC > x$draw_refit_hi
beyond_range <- function(x) {
  outside_range(x) & sign(x$draw_refit_lo) == sign(x$draw_refit_hi) &
    abs(x$naive_log2FC) > pmax(abs(x$draw_refit_lo), abs(x$draw_refit_hi))
}
f_out <- outside_range(f)
f_beyond <- beyond_range(f)
f204 <- fl("FLT1-204")
```

FLT1-214 has `r int(fl("FLT1-214")$mean_count)` reads on average and an InfRV of `r num(fl("FLT1-214")$mean_inf_rv, 1)`.
On the point counts its log2 fold-change is `r num(fl("FLT1-214")$naive_log2FC)`
(Wald interval `r num(fl("FLT1-214")$naive_ci_lo)` to `r num(fl("FLT1-214")$naive_ci_hi)`);
refitted on each Gibbs draw with the same model it lies between
`r num(fl("FLT1-214")$draw_refit_lo)` and `r num(fl("FLT1-214")$draw_refit_hi)`: the point estimate is larger than every refit.
Its direction is never in doubt, and it replicates in all `r int(fl("FLT1-214")$n_called_discovery)` half-splits that call it.
What is in doubt is the size of the effect: the point estimate and the refits disagree, and neither is the truth (see below).
FLT1-214 is not special within its gene: `r sum(f_out)` of the `r nrow(f)` tested FLT1 isoforms have a point estimate outside the range of their refits,
`r sum(f_beyond)` of them further from zero than the whole range.
The gap is negligible for the abundant ones (FLT1-204, `r num(f204$naive_log2FC, 3)` against `r num(f204$draw_refit_lo, 3)` to `r num(f204$draw_refit_hi, 3)`)
and can be much larger for those with a few hundred reads or fewer, up to `r num(val("B.posthoc.f1.flt1_214.outside_by"))` log2 units for FLT1-214,
though not for all of them (FLT1-212, with `r int(fl("FLT1-212")$mean_count)` reads, lies inside its range).
FLT1-204, with `r int(fl("FLT1-204")$mean_count)` reads, is the only FLT1 isoform in class `high`;
`r nrow(mod)` of the `r nrow(f)` tested isoforms are `moderate` because of their InfRV,
yet they replicate in `r pct(min(mod$replicated_when_called), 0)` to `r pct(max(mod$replicated_when_called), 0)`
of the half-splits that call them.
The class does not separate them.

FLT1-214 is not unique (a check added after the results were known).
Of the `r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.n_calls"))` transcript calls of the full comparison (q < 0.05),
`r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside_range.n"))` (`r pct(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside_range.share"))`) have a point fold-change
outside the range of their per-draw refits,
`r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside_by_gt_1.n"))` by more than one log2 unit, and
`r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside_by_ge_flt1_214.n"))` (`r pct(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside_by_ge_flt1_214.share"))`)
at least as far as FLT1-214 (`r num(val("B.posthoc.f1.flt1_214.outside_by"))` log2 units beyond the range).
LEP-203, an isoform of LEP (a gene-level example of the plan, below), comes close
(`r num(val("B.posthoc.f1.named.LEP-203.point"))` against `r num(val("B.posthoc.f1.named.LEP-203.draw_lo"))` to
`r num(val("B.posthoc.f1.named.LEP-203.draw_hi"))`, `r num(val("B.posthoc.f1.named.LEP-203.outside_by"))` log2 units beyond).
This is frequent in classes `moderate` and `low`
(`r pct(val("B.posthoc.f1.class_moderate.outside_range.share"))` and `r pct(val("B.posthoc.f1.class_low.outside_range.share"))`)
and rare in `high` (`r pct(val("B.posthoc.f1.class_high.outside_range.share"))`).
Two cautions apply.
For `r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside.wald_overlaps_range.n"))` of the `r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside_range.n"))`
the Wald interval of the point estimate overlaps the range of the refits,
and in `r int(val("B.posthoc.f1.outside.point_beyond_far_end.n"))` the point estimate is further from zero than the whole range:
the refits on the draws are pulled towards zero relative to the point estimate.
The point estimate comes from the EM algorithm (the most likely split of the reads) and the draws from a Gibbs sampler
(which averages over plausible splits), and the two differ systematically for poorly determined isoforms;
neither is ground truth, and these data cannot say which is closer to it.
The range of the refits is not a confidence interval for the point estimate.

### ENG and LEP

```{r}
#| label: story-numbers
sg_gene <- function(g) story[story$level == "gene" & story$gene_name %in% g, ]
sg_iso <- function(g) story[story$level == "isoform" & story$gene_name %in% g & story$tested_edgeR %in% TRUE, ]
sg_tx <- function(t) story[story$level == "isoform" & story$transcript_name %in% t, ]
rep_of <- function(x) paste0(int(x$n_called_discovery * x$replicated_when_called), " of ", int(x$n_called_discovery))
eng <- sg_iso("ENG")
lep <- sg_iso("LEP")
eng_all <- story[story$level == "isoform" & story$gene_name == "ENG", ]
eng_called <- eng[eng$naive_q < 0.05, ]
```

At gene level both are clear: ENG has a log2 fold-change of `r num(sg_gene("ENG")$naive_log2FC)`
(refits on the draws `r num(sg_gene("ENG")$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(sg_gene("ENG")$draw_refit_hi)`) and replicates in
`r rep_of(sg_gene("ENG"))` of the directed pairs that call it; LEP has `r num(sg_gene("LEP")$naive_log2FC)`
(`r num(sg_gene("LEP")$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(sg_gene("LEP")$draw_refit_hi)`) and replicates in `r rep_of(sg_gene("LEP"))`.
The isoforms tell the same story as FLT1.
ENG has `r nrow(eng_all)` expressed isoforms, of which `r nrow(eng)` were tested and `r nrow(eng_called)` called at q < 0.05;
only `r sum(eng$confidence == "high")` of the tested ones is in class `high`.
Its two most abundant isoforms are in class `low`, yet replicate whenever called:
ENG-202 (`r int(sg_tx("ENG-202")$mean_count)` reads, `r rep_of(sg_tx("ENG-202"))`) and
ENG-216 (`r int(sg_tx("ENG-216")$mean_count)` reads, `r rep_of(sg_tx("ENG-216"))`).
`r sum(outside_range(eng))` of the `r nrow(eng)` tested ENG isoforms have a point estimate outside the range of their refits,
for example ENG-255 (`r num(sg_tx("ENG-255")$naive_log2FC)` against `r num(sg_tx("ENG-255")$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(sg_tx("ENG-255")$draw_refit_hi)`, `r int(sg_tx("ENG-255")$mean_count)` reads).
All `r nrow(lep)` LEP isoforms are called and replicate whenever called, two of them in class `low`;
`r sum(outside_range(lep))` lie outside the range of their refits, LEP-201 on the side nearer zero
(`r num(sg_tx("LEP-201")$naive_log2FC)` against `r num(sg_tx("LEP-201")$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(sg_tx("LEP-201")$draw_refit_hi)`),
so the gap does not always go the same way.

### The fragile and the robust rule

```{r}
#| label: rule-numbers
rule_row <- function(pattern) story[story$level == "gene" & grepl(pattern, story$rule, fixed = TRUE), ]
r_frag <- rule_row("fragile (prereg rule)")
r_task <- rule_row("fragile (WP-B plan rule")
r_rob <- rule_row("robust (prereg rule)")
las <- sg_tx("LAS1L-202")
tbc <- sg_tx("TBC1D26-204")
```

The plan's fragile rule asked for the gene with the most isoform calls (q < 0.05) that are all outside class `high`
and are supported (same sign, one-sided p < 0.05) in fewer than half of the `r int(val("design.directed_pairs"))` validation halves
(the plan's "held-out support"; for a call on the whole cohort these halves are not held out,
because the sign comes from all `r int(val("design.n_pe") + val("design.n_control_units"))` samples and every half is part of them).
No gene qualified (`r int(r_frag$n_candidates)` candidates), so it picked none.
A substitute rule, defined in the analysis scripts and not in the plan (post hoc amendment A20),
takes the switch or productive-fraction result with the smallest p-value among genes with a gene-level call (q < 0.05),
keeping only results whose test, refitted on each draw, is significant in fewer than half of the draws.
It picked `r r_task$gene_name` out of `r int(r_task$n_candidates)` candidate results (switch or productive-fraction tests; a gene can contribute more than one).
At gene level its point log2 fold-change is `r num(r_task$naive_log2FC)` (q = `r num(r_task$naive_q, 3)`),
while only `r pct(r_task$sign_agree, 0)` of the refits on the draws share its sign
(`r num(r_task$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(r_task$draw_refit_hi)`),
yet the gene call replicates in `r rep_of(r_task)` of the pairs that call it.
Its isoform LAS1L-202 (`r int(las$mean_count)` reads, class `r las$confidence`) has a point log2 fold-change of
`r num(las$naive_log2FC)` against refits of `r num(las$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(las$draw_refit_hi)`
(`r pct(las$sign_agree, 0)` with the sign of the point estimate), and replicates in `r rep_of(las)`.
So the gene that looks most fragile by the draws replicates well in the held-out halves.
That is not a contradiction: the held-out halves are quantified by the same EM algorithm,
so replication cannot tell a real change from a distortion of the quantification that repeats in every sample.
It is a reminder that a flag that predicts replication on average says little about a single gene.
(The sign agreement in this section is the share of edgeR refits on the draws with the sign of the point estimate,
not the `sign_agreement` of `de_confidence()`.)

The plan's robust rule asked for the gene with the smallest gene-level q-value whose top isoform is in class `high`
and is supported in at least 90% of the same validation halves (again not held out for a call on the whole cohort).
It picked `r r_rob$gene_name` out of `r int(r_rob$n_candidates)` candidate genes, a gene with a single expressed isoform.
At gene level its log2 fold-change is `r num(r_rob$naive_log2FC)` (refits `r num(r_rob$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(r_rob$draw_refit_hi)`),
replicated in `r rep_of(r_rob)` of the pairs that call it;
its only expressed isoform, TBC1D26-204, has `r num(tbc$naive_log2FC)` (refits `r num(tbc$draw_refit_lo)` to `r num(tbc$draw_refit_hi)`),
replicated in `r rep_of(tbc)`.

## What we recommend

- **Report `sign_agreement` next to every isoform call you interpret** (`de_confidence()`),
  and look again at calls below 0.95. In these data they were a small share of calls that replicated
  about half as often as the rest (`r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_flagged"))` against `r pct(val("B.flags.flag_unstable.rate_unflagged"))`).
  Do not read a value above 0.95 as a clean bill: the flag marked only `r pct(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.sensitivity_nonreplication"), 0)`
  of the calls that failed to replicate, and false calls driven by biological variability are mostly stable over the draws.
- **Do not filter on the confidence class.** It marks most calls and separates them only modestly beyond count and test statistic,
  so a filter on it would discard most calls that replicate,
  and in the null, at equal removal, it removed no more false calls than dropping the least expressed transcripts.
  (This advice led the package to remove the class; it is kept here as the record of the evaluation.)
- **Do not use the InfRV cut-off of 0.5 as a filter on a genome-wide human annotation**; it marks nearly every expressed isoform.
- **With 3 to 5 samples per group, expect nominal false positives (p < 0.01) to fall more often on uncertain isoforms**,
  and check the uncertainty of each isoform you interpret; at q < 0.05 edgeR on point counts made at most
  `r num(max(sapply(c("3v3", "5v5", "7v7"), function(d) val(paste0("A.mean_calls_q05.", d, ".M1.own.all")))))` false calls per null split at any size tested.
  Divided counts (`scale_counts()`) remove the concentration but not the false calls, and in the null they cost power;
  in the real comparison they made more calls on the same transcripts, of unknown truth.
- **With 7 samples per group, the largest size tested, edgeR on point counts was calibrated here at q < 0.05** (`r num(val("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M1.own.all"), 3)` false calls per null split); no concentration of false calls in uncertain isoforms was detected, though the conservative interval cannot rule one out, and accounting for uncertainty mostly cost power.
  This is a result for edgeR's quasi-likelihood test (and limma-voom): the DESeq2 Wald test on the same counts made many more false calls.
- **For low-count isoforms, do not quote the point fold-change alone.**
  What was evaluated here is the primary model (edgeR) refitted on each draw.
  When the point estimate lies outside the range of those refits, report both and treat the size of the effect as uncertain;
  neither number is the true one.
  The `lfc_median`, `lfc_lo` and `lfc_hi` of `de_confidence()` come from a simpler statistic
  (the difference between the groups of the mean of log2 counts with a pseudocount of 5, a log ratio of geometric means), which pulls low-count fold-changes towards zero.
  They were not compared with the point estimate in this evaluation, so a gap between the two is expected
  for low counts and is not by itself a sign of a problem.

After this evaluation the package removed the confidence class and now reports `unstable` (sign agreement below 0.95) as the flag of a call,
keeping InfRV, ambiguity and identifiability as descriptions of the isoform.
This change follows the results above and was not part of the plan;
the flag catches about `r pct(val("B.5_ppv_cost_flag_unstable.sensitivity_nonreplication"), 0)` of the calls that do not replicate.
The [uncertainty article](isoformic-uncertainty.html) shows the current columns.

## Every method in the null {#every-method-in-the-null}

The main text follows edgeR. These tables give every expression method that the placenta null ran,
including those that do not fit the story told above.
Intervals are the delete-one-unit jackknife (Monte Carlo corrected where valid, raw otherwise;
the type of each is in the bundled table). Intervals are cut at the lowest possible value, so counts often have a lower end of 0.
The rate ratio was computed only for the methods it is shown for, and its interval here is the primary one;
the wider raw jackknife intervals are in the figure of the rate ratios above.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-null-all
null_method <- c(
  M1 = "edgeR QL, point counts",
  M2 = "edgeR QL, divided counts",
  M3 = "limma-voom, point counts",
  M4 = "limma-voom, divided counts",
  M5 = "DESeq2 Wald, point counts",
  M6 = "swish, draws",
  M7 = "swish, every draw set to the point counts (control)",
  M8 = "Wilcoxon, log CPM",
  M9a = "edgeR, point counts, class high only",
  M9b = "edgeR, point counts, without uncertain or ambiguous",
  M10a = "edgeR, point counts, as many low-expression transcripts removed as M9a",
  M10b = "edgeR, point counts, as many low-expression transcripts removed as M9b",
  M11raw = "edgeR QL, gene level, point counts",
  M11div = "edgeR QL, gene level, divided counts"
)
has <- function(key) any(ev$key == key)
ci_or_dash <- function(key) {
  r <- get_row(key)
  # three decimals for the small values, so that they match the text
  digits <- if (abs(r$estimate) < 1) 3 else 2
  if (is.na(r$ci_lo) || is.na(r$ci_hi)) {
    return(num(r$estimate, digits))
  }
  ci(key, digits)
}
null_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("7v7", "5v5", "3v3"), function(d) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(null_method), function(m) {
    k_calls <- paste0("A.mean_calls_q05.", d, ".", m, ".own.all")
    if (!has(k_calls)) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    k_inf <- paste0("A.inflation_p01.", d, ".", m, ".own.all")
    data.frame(
      Size = sub("v", " v ", d, fixed = TRUE),
      Method = null_method[[m]],
      Splits = int(get_row(k_calls)$n),
      `False calls per split, q < 0.05` = ci_or_dash(k_calls),
      `Observed over expected, p < 0.01` = ci_or_dash(k_inf),
      `Rate ratio, top against bottom third of InfRV` = if (has(rr(d, m))) ci(rr(d, m)) else "",
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(null_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

DESeq2 was run on `r int(get_row("A.mean_calls_q05.7v7.M5.own.all")$n)` splits at 7 v 7 and,
in the pilot only, on `r int(get_row("A.mean_calls_q05.5v5.M5.own.all")$n)` splits at 5 and at 3 per group, so its small-sample rows rest on very few splits.
Gene-level rows count genes, not transcripts.
With 3 samples per group the Wilcoxon test cannot reach p < 0.01.
The filtered methods (M9 and M10) remove calls after the test, so their observed over expected share is low by construction.
The swish control (M7) is a diagnostic, not a calibrated reference: on 30 identical copies of the counts,
the permutation p-values of `swish` pile up at some values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-thinning-all
thin_all <- c(
  M1 = "edgeR QL, point counts",
  M2 = "edgeR QL, divided counts",
  M6 = "swish, draws",
  M9a = "edgeR, point counts, class high only",
  M10a = "edgeR, point counts, as many low-expression transcripts removed as M9a"
)
thin_all_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("7v7_louo", "5v5"), function(d) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(thin_all), function(m) {
    base <- paste0("A.thin.", d, ".", m, ".all.q_0.05.")
    top <- paste0("A.thin.", d, ".", m, ".top_tertile.q_0.05.")
    data.frame(
      Size = if (d == "5v5") "5 v 5" else "7 v 7",
      Method = thin_all[[m]],
      `Empirical FDR` = ci(paste0(base, "fdr_pooled"), 3),
      `True calls` = int(val(paste0(base, "total_calls")) - val(paste0(base, "total_false"))),
      `True calls, top third of InfRV` = int(val(paste0(top, "total_calls")) - val(paste0(top, "total_false"))),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(thin_all_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: thin-fdr-5v5
thin5 <- lapply(names(thin_all), function(m) get_row(paste0("A.thin.5v5.", m, ".all.q_0.05.fdr_pooled")))
thin5_est <- vapply(thin5, function(r) r$estimate, numeric(1))
thin5_hi <- vapply(thin5, function(r) r$ci_hi, numeric(1))
```

The power arm at 5 v 5 tells the same story as at 7 v 7: the empirical false discovery rate of every method is
between `r pct(min(thin5_est))` and `r pct(max(thin5_est))`, below 5%, though the upper ends of the intervals reach
`r pct(max(thin5_hi), 0)`; point counts find the most true changes, most of all in the top third of InfRV (q < 0.05, `r int(get_row("A.thin.5v5.M1.all.q_0.05.fdr_pooled")$n)` splits per size).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-robustness
robust <- c(
  "the other member of each A/B pair" = "variant_member",
  "haplotype copies not folded" = "variant_unfolded"
)
rob_row <- function(label, key_all, key_high, key_low, ref = NULL) {
  data.frame(
    Variant = label,
    Splits = int(get_row(key_all)$n),
    `All transcripts` = ci(key_all),
    `Top third of InfRV` = if (is.null(key_high)) "" else ci(key_high),
    `Bottom third of InfRV` = if (is.null(key_low)) "" else ci(key_low),
    `Main run on the same splits` = if (is.null(ref)) "" else ci(ref),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
rk <- function(v, s) paste0("A.robust.", v, ".M1.", s)
rob_tab <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(robust), function(lab) {
    v <- robust[[lab]]
    rob_row(
      lab, rk(v, "all.all"), rk(v, "infrv_tertile.high"), rk(v, "infrv_tertile.low"),
      rk(paste0("main_run_on_the_splits_of_", v), "all.all")
    )
  })),
  rob_row(
    "splits drawn without balancing sex", rk("7v7_unrestricted_sex", "all.all"),
    rk("7v7_unrestricted_sex", "infrv_tertile.high"), rk("7v7_unrestricted_sex", "infrv_tertile.low")
  ),
  rob_row(
    "main run, only splits with the same sex counts in both groups", rk("7v7_with_equal_sex_counts", "all.all"),
    rk("7v7_with_equal_sex_counts", "infrv_tertile.high"), rk("7v7_with_equal_sex_counts", "infrv_tertile.low")
  ),
  rob_row("main run, chrX and chrY transcripts removed", rk("7v7_without_chrX_chrY_transcripts", "chr_xy.FALSE"), NULL, NULL)
)
knitr::kable(rob_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

The robustness variants of the 7 v 7 null give the observed over expected share of false calls at p < 0.01
for edgeR on point counts. In the column of all transcripts the share stays below or near 1 and every interval includes 1.
One interval elsewhere in the table excludes 1: the top third of InfRV in the splits drawn without balancing sex,
`r ci(rk("7v7_unrestricted_sex", "infrv_tertile.high"))`, which is fewer false calls than expected, not more.
A variant on draws 16 to 30 changes only the methods that use the draws; for point counts it is identical by construction,
and its effect on the other methods is not in the bundled tables.

## Limits

- One real biological contrast (placenta, `r int(val("design.n_pe"))` against `r int(val("design.n_control"))`
  samples, analysed as `r int(val("design.n_control_units"))` independent control units)
  and one biological null in another species (mouse, with a hidden batch). Long reads were not tested.
- Replication between half-splits of one cohort is agreement between subsets of the same samples, not truth, and it depends on power.
  None of the intervals of the held-out replication includes the variation from the choice of samples.
- The read halves are a technical check of the noise the draws model, on few calls.
  There, the former default class flags almost every call and its odds ratios are degenerate (quasi-separation), so they are not quoted.
- Not pre-registered: the choice of sign agreement as the main result (its threshold was), the group size at which R-A was judged,
  the p < 0.01 event of the R-A rate ratio (the plan listed p and q thresholds without choosing one),
  the q < 0.10 discovery rule and its fallback, the small-sample excess as a finding,
  the covariates of the R-B odds ratio (count, |z|, number of isoforms of the gene, type class),
  the replication-rate difference on which "beats the count-matched flag" was judged,
  the mouse batch analysis, the gene-clustered intervals, the pair fixed effects, the spline adjustment,
  the same-size controls of the sign-agreement flag,
  the matched deficit within cells of the joint deciles of count and |z| (the plan defines only the replication metric and three controls),
  the sign-concordance outcome (same sign in the held-out half, without the p threshold) and its odds ratio,
  the point-against-draws check, the gene (not transcript) unit of the planned bootstrap,
  the comparison of the read-half flags, the substitute fragile rule that picked LAS1L,
  and the mouse null itself (its dataset and 5 v 5 design; only the R-A rule and model applied to it were registered).
- R-B was judged against a control (the lowest-count calls) that differs from the count-matched flag the plan described.
  The plan's placebo flag ("a random flag of the same size per split") was implemented as the default flag shuffled
  within cells of equal count and |z|, and its permutation baseline of the labels is not a null with
  `r int(val("design.n_pe") / 2)` preeclampsia samples per discovery half, so it was reported but not used;
  both departures were recorded only after the results.
- The plan and its amendments are kept in the package repository, not in an external registry,
  and were committed together with the results; that the plan came first rests on the time stamp inside it.
  The 9 pilot splits of the null were run before the design amendment and are part of the reported results
  (the only ones for DESeq2 at 5 and 3 per group).
- Several Monte Carlo corrected placenta intervals are much narrower than the raw jackknife; the raw intervals are given where it matters.
- All reported calls use 30 draws; subsets of 15 draws were used only as stability checks, and more draws (100 or more) were not tested for the calls.
  Only the prior of the overdispersion was computed from 100 draws, in a knockdown series, where it was
  `r pc(100 * (val("D.5_prior_ratio_100_first_30_draws_3_g100_runs") - 1))` higher than from 30.
- The numbers come from a frozen snapshot of the package code, not from the current development version.
  The sign agreement of the current `de_confidence()` was recomputed on the discovery half of all `r int(val("B.pkgcheck.pairs"))` directed pairs
  (`92_package_flag_check.R`, a post hoc check of the code, amendment A24): its `unstable` flag differs from the evaluated one
  on `r int(val("B.pkgcheck.unstable_disagree"))` of `r int(get_row("B.pkgcheck.unstable_disagree")$n)` assessed calls,
  and from the flag scored in the replication table on `r int(val("B.pkgcheck.pooled_flag_disagree"))` of `r int(val("B.pkgcheck.pooled_rows"))`,
  so the replication results above describe the current `unstable` flag (rerun that script after a change to `de_confidence()`);
  the class columns (`confidence` in the tables of FLT1, ENG, LEP and LAS1L) are those of the evaluated snapshot.
- The package's flag is a secondary flag of this analysis, made the headline after the results:
  its effect in another cohort, with another primary test (DESeq2, swish) or with other replicates (bootstrap, long reads) is an out-of-sample question.

## Reproducing these numbers

The scripts are in `data-raw/uncertainty_evidence/` of the package repository, numbered in the order they run;
the header of each gives its inputs, settings and memory, and `prereg.yaml` and `prereg_amendments.yaml` give the plan and its changes.
`90_article_tables.R` copies every number into four small tables, which this article reads:

```{r}
#| label: tables
#| echo: true
data_dir <- "data/uncertainty_evidence" # vignettes/articles/data/uncertainty_evidence in the source repository
ev <- read_parquet(file.path(data_dir, "evidence_numbers.parquet"))
ev[ev$key == "B.flags.flag_unstable.adjusted_or", c("key", "estimate", "ci_lo", "ci_hi", "ci_type", "source")]
```
